# Phase C error corpus -- lexer rejections (jslex.c).
# ERRORS.md section 12, rows 251-276. Every snippet MUST error in the C build in
# at least one of flags=0 / flags=JS_STRICT. No try/catch here on purpose.
#
# NOTE ON ESCAPES: the harness rewrites backslash+n -> newline and backslash+t ->
# tab BEFORE compiling. So `'a\nb'` below is a string literal containing a RAW
# newline (which is what row 258 needs), and a line ending in a lone backslash is
# a backslash at EOF (row 256). Sequences that must survive as two characters are
# built with String.fromCharCode instead.

# --- row 251: jsY_unescape -- "unexpected escape sequence" (identifiers) ---
var \x41 = 1
var \u041 = 1
var \uZZZZ = 1
var \u00 = 1
var a\u12 = 1
var \q = 1
var o = {}; o.\x41
var o = {}; o.\u12g4

# --- row 252: lexhex -- "malformed hexadecimal number" ---
0x
0X
var a = 0x
var a = 0X
0x.5
var a = 0xg
0x + 1
var a = 0X;

# --- row 253: lexnumber -- "number with leading zero" (legacy octal) ---
010
00
08
09
var a = 0123
0777 + 1
var a = [01]
01.5

# --- row 254: lexnumber -- "missing exponent" ---
1e
1E
1e+
1e-
1.5e
0.1E+
var a = 12e
var a = .5e-
1e+ + 1

# --- row 255: lexnumber -- "number with letter suffix" ---
123abc
1_0
1$
3.14foo
1e5x
var a = 5n
var a = 1if
# lexhex returns TK_NUMBER before the letter-suffix check, so a hex literal with a
# trailing letter falls through to the parser's "expected ';'" instead (row 279).
0x1g
0xFFq
var a = 1.2.3

# --- row 265: jsY_lexx -- "unexpected character: '%c'" (printable ASCII) ---

`

1 @ 2
;;;@
